ground_truth.name: <runtime this[currChildName]>
ground_truth.note: defaultVisit is never called by its own name anywhere in packages/chevrotain/src - `rg -n "defaultVisit" packages/chevrotain/src` returns only its own declaration (cst_visitor.ts:4), an explanatory comment (line 19), and one ASSIGNMENT (not a call) at cst_visitor.ts:90: `withDefaultsProto[ruleName] = defaultVisit;`, inside createBaseVisitorConstructorWithDefaults. That assignment installs defaultVisit as the value of every rule-named property on a base-visitor prototype object; it is invoked later, if at all, only through `this[currChildName](...)` (cst_visitor.ts:15, inside defaultVisit's own body, for nested CST children) or `this[cstNode.name](...)` (cst_visitor.ts:49, inside the sibling `visit` function's closure) - both fully runtime-string-keyed dispatches where the property name comes from parsed grammar data (a CstNode's `.name`), not from any static identifier in this source tree. typescript-language-server's find-references draft reported the cst_visitor.ts:90 assignment as a 'caller', which is a false positive of exactly the kind flagged by the user brief: a real, correctly-located reference to the right symbol that is not a call at all.

verification.verification_note: ADVERSARIAL. All 3 classes above extend GAstVisitor (packages/gast/src/visitor.ts, outside packages/chevrotain/src and therefore not itself a candidate, but read for verification). GAstVisitor.visit(node) (visitor.ts:16) dispatches by AST node-kind string with `return this.visitOption(nodeAny)` at visitor.ts:24 when node.constructor.name === "Option" - i.e. every call to `someVisitorInstance.visit(optionNode)` anywhere in the codebase reaches *whichever* of the 3 same-named visitOption overrides belongs to the concrete class of `someVisitorInstance`, which is not decidable from the call site's source text (it depends on which of the 3 collector classes was `new`'d earlier in the same function). This is structurally identical to the trait-default-dispatch pattern already validated in hyperfine-12 (MarkupExporter::table_header) and hyperfine-38 (Exporter::serialize) for Rust, here reproduced via TypeScript's own `this[methodName]`-free but equally dynamic single-dispatch-through-a-common-base-class-visit()-method idiom. Framed as `tasks.callers.ambiguous` (mirroring the shape SCHEMA.md defines for `tasks.callees.ambiguous`) rather than `tasks.callees.ambiguous`, because here the ambiguity is about who legitimately reaches *this* implementation, and the true dispatcher (`GAstVisitor.visit`) lives outside packages/chevrotain/src and so cannot itself be the golden-set symbol under the scope restriction for this repo.

ground_truth.name: <grammar-author-supplied ALT callback>
ground_truth.note: `chosenAlternative.ALT.call(this)` at recognizer_engine.ts:658. `ALT` is a property of one element of the `alts`/`altsOrOpts.DEF` array that RecognizerApi's OR/OR1..OR9 methods (recognizer_api.ts:322 onward) pass straight through from whatever grammar the parser's end user wrote (e.g. `this.OR([{ ALT: () => this.SUBRULE(this.someRule) }, ...])`), entirely outside packages/chevrotain/src. There is no finite, enumerable candidate list: unlike defaultVisit's `this[name]()` (still bounded, in principle, by the grammar's own rule names), each `ALT` here is an arbitrary function value with no name at all to look up - not even a runtime string key, just an opaque closure reference threaded through 3 layers of parameter passing (OR -> orInternal -> chosenAlternative.ALT).

impact.note: No enumerable depth-1 target exists; the callee is an opaque external closure (see verification_note).

verification.verification_method: Direct reading of source files via the Read tool, with ripgrep used only to enumerate candidate line numbers (never corbel) which were then individually opened and read in context to confirm each is a real call and to identify its enclosing function. corbel was never executed to produce any answer in this file. Draft candidates and caller lists were first generated by benchmarks/goldenset/lsp_to_draft.py (typescript-language-server, tsserver from a locally installed typescript package since the cloned repo has no node_modules), then every caller line was independently cross-checked against ripgrep output and manually read before being accepted or rejected.
verification.verification_note: ADVERSARIAL. This is the concrete implementation behind every OR/OR1..OR9 DSL method (recognizer_api.ts:322-420ish, all thin wrappers delegating to `this.orInternal(...)`), matching the OR item named in the task brief. `rg -n "\.ALT\b"` finds the callee-invocation site trivially (line 658) but confirms there is no in-repo function definition it could be attributed to - `ALT` callbacks are pure external data.

ground_truth.name: <grammar-author-supplied MANY/AT_LEAST_ONE action callback>
ground_truth.note: `action.call(this)` at recognizer_engine.ts:638. `action` is resolved a few lines earlier from `actionORMethodDef` - either the bare callback passed directly to MANY/AT_LEAST_ONE (`actionORMethodDef` itself, when it is a function) or its `.DEF` property (when the caller instead passed a `{ DEF, GATE }` options object) - in both cases a callback supplied by the grammar author calling the MANY/AT_LEAST_ONE DSL methods, entirely outside packages/chevrotain/src (recognizer_api.ts's MANY/AT_LEAST_ONE/AT_LEAST_ONE_SEP methods, mirroring OR, forward their argument straight through to manyInternalLogic/atLeastOneInternalLogic without inspecting it). doSingleRepetition itself is called from 3 sites within RecognizerEngine (lines ~400, ~405 in atLeastOneInternalLogic, and line 526 in manyInternalLogic), but the identity of `action` at each is a distinct external, unnamed closure with no finite candidate set.

impact.note: Only manyInternalLogic's call (line 526) hand-traced for depth-1 impact; atLeastOneInternalLogic's 2 calls (~lines 400, 405) were located by rg but not individually re-read within this session's time budget.

Draft candidates and caller lists were first generated by benchmarks/goldenset/lsp_to_draft.py (typescript-language-server, tsserver from a locally installed typescript package since the cloned repo has no node_modules), then every caller line was independently cross-checked against ripgrep output and manually read before being accepted or rejected.
verification.verification_note: ADVERSARIAL. Distinct from orInternal's ALT.call: this is the shared implementation backing MANY/MANY_SEP/AT_LEAST_ONE/AT_LEAST_ONE_SEP (the second half of the "OR/MANY/OPTION/AT_LEAST_ONE" higher-order-callback family named in the task brief), reached via manyInternalLogic (line 502) and (by the same action.call(this) shape, not separately entered here) atLeastOneInternalLogic. `doSingleRepetition`'s own 3 in-repo callers (all within RecognizerEngine) are statically enumerable and NOT ambiguous; the ambiguity is specifically in what `action` resolves to at the moment doSingleRepetition invokes it.
